which runtime implements the accepted-not-implemented rules (current server or PR #1)

note: What a caller may rely on when it asks the communication boundary to deliver a message. Accepted by the owner on 2026-10-16. Rules marked current are served by platform-notifications-api today; rules marked accepted-not-implemented are accepted policy that no runtime implements yet and must be implemented before any cutover. This repository serves none of these routes.

operations.idempotency: dedupe_key; a repeat returns outcome=existing with the first entry unchanged (concurrent repeats keep the first)
not idempotent: each delivered/failed call counts one attempt; callers retry only 5xx, at most 3 times
event_id; a replayed provider event returns existing

retry.delivery_semantics: at-least-once (a result that cannot be recorded may be resent next run)
retry.provider_idempotency_key_derivation: line: uuid5(fixed namespace, 'message/<notification id>'), identical on every retry; LINE honours it for 24 h
retry.email_message_id: stable '<message/<id>@...>' for hygiene only; SMTP does not deduplicate on it, so an uncertain retry can duplicate

opt_out.enforced_by: the communication boundary before any provider call; callers never filter themselves
opt_out.suppressed_result: entry stays undelivered with delivery_error=opted_out and no attempt counted
opt_out.inbound_rules: each unfollow in a LINE batch is its own opt-out with its own recipient (source.userId); an unfollow without webhookEventId or userId is rejected with 400

privacy.recipient: callers pass an opaque recipient_ref; addresses and provider credentials stay inside the boundary
privacy.errors: provider errors are reduced to a short code (e.g. telegram_http_403); URLs that embed tokens are never logged

status_values.accepted-not-implemented: accepted by the owner 2026-10-16, not implemented by any runtime
